references.text: David expresses his one desire: to dwell in the Lord's house all the days of his life. This reflects the idea of 'the one thing necessary' that Jesus points to – choosing fellowship with God above all else.
The psalmist declares that he has no other than God in heaven, and that nothing on earth can compare with Him. This reflects the 'good portion' Mary chose – God's presence as the highest good.
Context for the verse: Martha welcomes Jesus and is busy with all the preparations, while Mary sits at Jesus' feet and listens. Jesus rebukes Martha and says that Mary has chosen the good portion.
The demon-possessed man in Gerasa was found sitting at Jesus' feet after being healed. Sitting at Jesus' feet symbolizes discipleship and fellowship with Him, just as Mary did.
Mary and Martha of Bethany are mentioned again in John, where Mary anoints Jesus' feet. Her devotion to Jesus confirms that she chose 'the good portion'.

Jesus says: 'Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures and gives eternal life.' This reflects the contrast between Martha's worry about earthly things and Mary's choice of spiritual things.
'Seek first God's kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.' Jesus prioritizes the spiritual over the material, just as He does with Martha and Mary.

The apostles choose to prioritize prayer and the ministry of the Word over practical tasks like serving at tables. The principle is the same: the spiritual takes precedence, just as Mary chose to listen to Jesus' words.
Paul counts everything as loss compared to knowing Christ Jesus. This attitude reflects Mary's choice of 'the good portion' – knowledge of Jesus as the highest good that cannot be taken from her.

The warning not to reject Him who speaks points to the importance of listening to God's Word. Mary chose to listen to Jesus, and this would not be taken from her – whoever listens to the Lord's words chooses what endures.
